title: CELPIP Writing: The Email & the Survey
summary: CELPIP's two writing tasks — an email and a survey response, 150–200 words each — and the structure that scores well.

nodes.label: Task 1: Email
nodes.note: Write an email for a real situation (150–200 words)

nodes.label: Task 2: Survey
nodes.note: Choose an option & justify it (150–200 words)

nodes.label: Purpose + tone
nodes.note: Match the situation and the reader

chunks.heading: Task 1 — Writing an Email
chunks.body: You're given a **situation** and write an **email of 150–200 words**. Cover **all the points asked**, use an **appropriate greeting, purpose, body and close**, and match the **tone** to the reader (formal to a manager, friendly to a friend). Addressing every required point is essential.
chunks.realExample: If the task says explain the problem, say what you want, and suggest a time, your email must do all three — missing one point costs marks even if the writing is fluent.
chunks.memoryHook: Greeting → purpose → all the points → close. Match the tone to the reader.

chunks.heading: Task 2 — Responding to Survey Questions
chunks.body: You read a **survey with options**, **choose one**, and write **150–200 words justifying your choice** (and often why not the other). It's a mini opinion piece: **state your choice, give clear reasons with examples, and stay on topic**.
chunks.realExample: Survey: should a community centre add a gym or a library? Pick one, give two concrete reasons (health, cost, who benefits), and briefly note why the other is weaker — a tidy, reasoned response.
chunks.memoryHook: Pick an option, give 2 reasons + examples, note why not the other. Stay in 150–200 words.

chunks.heading: Correct, organised, on-topic
chunks.body: Human raters reward **clear organisation, correct grammar and vocabulary, and fully addressing the task** over fancy language. Use **paragraphs**, connect ideas with simple linkers, and leave time to **reread for errors**.
chunks.realExample: Two short, well-organised paragraphs with correct grammar beat one long paragraph with impressive but error-filled sentences — clarity and completeness win.
chunks.memoryHook: Organised + correct + complete beats fancy. Paragraphs, linkers, then proofread.

chunks.heading: Mind the word count and the clock
chunks.body: Aim for **150–200 words per task** — too short looks underdeveloped, too long risks errors and running out of time. Plan for **~30 seconds to outline**, write, and save a **minute to check** spelling and grammar.
chunks.realExample: Finish with a minute left? Reread for subject-verb agreement, articles and spelling — the exact slips human raters notice.
chunks.memoryHook: 150–200 words. Quick outline, write, then a final grammar/spelling check.

recall.q: What are the two CELPIP writing tasks and the word count for each?
recall.a: Task 1 is writing an email and Task 2 is responding to survey questions — each 150–200 words.

recall.q: What must Task 1 (the email) include to score well?
recall.a: All the points asked, an appropriate greeting/purpose/body/close, and a tone matched to the reader.

recall.q: What do you do in Task 2 (the survey)?
recall.a: Choose one option and justify it in 150–200 words with clear reasons and examples, often noting why not the alternative.

recall.q: What do the human raters reward most?
recall.a: Clear organisation, correct grammar and vocabulary, and fully addressing the task — over fancy language.

recall.q: Why aim for 150–200 words rather than writing much more?
recall.a: Too short looks underdeveloped; too long risks more errors and running out of time.
